target.name: Unlimited Industries
target.founder: Alex Modon, Jordan Stern, Tara Viswanathan

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $12M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Unlimited Industries is a seed-stage housing and construction company founded by Alex Modon, Jordan Stern, and Tara Viswanathan, having raised $12M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a private comparables set of five frontier-tech construction players—BotBuilt, Apis Cor, Ground Control Development, ADMARES, and Hedral—with no applicable public market comparables in this nascent sector.

Given the single-stage nature of available data, stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach. Using total capital raised ($12M) as a baseline value proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement, the analysis derives an implied valuation of $30M. This method reflects market expectations for capital efficiency and product-market progress between funding rounds in frontier construction technology.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, with a median point of $30M. The 26% spread between low and high estimates reflects inherent uncertainty in mapping a single comparable methodology across the frontier-tech construction landscape, where exit multiples and round-stage progressions remain less established than in mature software sectors. Key uncertainties include the true revenue or unit economics of peer companies, the pace of product development validation, and whether Unlimited Industries' specific technical approach warrants premium or discount positioning within the peer set.
